newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower, gas firm leads losers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower, gas firm leads losers.

text.p: Colombian shares ended lower in trading that saw gas distribution company Promigas lead losers with a sharp drop in Bogota, dealers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell a paper-thin 0.01 percent to close at 16,539.43 on lower-than-average trading volume of about 1.1 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB dropped 0.14 percent, ending at 1,065.15 on above-average volume of nearly 8.5 billion pesos.
Volume in Bogota was fueled, at least in part, by a huge cross-trade involving shares of Promigas, the main gas distribution company on Colombia's Caribbean coast.
"The deal involved share swaps and operations among the current partners (in Promigas) and it didn't really affect the Bogota index," one broker said.
"The fall in the price was precisely because it was agreed in advance," he added, saying a large block of shares traded at below market value.
Such deals are not uncommon in Colombia, where the transparency of equity markets has often been called into question.
Promigas, which is partly owned by Enron Corp closed 9.26 percent lower at 3,720 pesos per share.

Other losers included brewing giant Bavaria, which fell 0.44 percent in Medellin to end at 6,800 pesos per share. The stock also trended lower in Bogota. Brokers cited concern about a company announcement regarding a proposed share split that will be formalized next month.
Banco de Bogota closed 0.80 percent lower in Bogota at 6,150 pesos per share on news shareholders failed to approve a proposed dividend because of adverse tax implications.
The day's few winners include Banco Ganadero, which rose 0.89 percent in Bogota to end at 340 pesos per share.
